questions.q: What does Salesforce call the flow type covered in this lesson, on the New Flow screen?
options: Schedule-Triggered Flow
Record-Triggered Flow
Platform Event-Triggered Flow
Autolaunched Flow (No Trigger)
questions.explain: Setup's New Flow screen lists this flow type as Schedule-Triggered Flow: it launches at a specified time and frequency.

questions.q: What does the Start element's Set Schedule option configure?
options: Which object the flow runs against
The start date, start time, and frequency (Once, Daily, or Weekly)
The flow's fault connector
The Activate button's permissions
questions.explain: Set Schedule is where you pick the date, time, and how often the flow repeats.

questions.q: What happens when a scheduled flow's Choose Object (Optional) is set, with entry conditions, instead of left blank?
options: The flow becomes a screen flow
The flow can no longer run on a schedule
The flow runs once for every matching record at the scheduled time, as a batch
The flow requires a user to click a button first
questions.explain: Choosing an object and conditions turns the scheduled flow into a batch job: it runs once per matching record, not once total.

questions.q: According to this lesson's example, what did the daily scheduled flow do at 1:00 AM?
options: Displayed a screen to the logged-in admin
Waited for a platform event message
Deleted all Opportunity records
Got high-priority Cases, counted them, and created an archived metric record
questions.explain: The worked example queried high-priority Cases, counted them with an Assignment element, and created an archive record — all without a trigger.

questions.q: Why would an admin reach for a scheduled flow instead of a record-triggered flow?
options: Record-triggered flows cannot create records
The automation depends on time passing, not on any single record being saved
Scheduled flows are the only flow type that can run Apex
Scheduled flows can show a screen but record-triggered flows cannot
questions.explain: Record-triggered flows only fire at a save moment; automation like “every record 30 days old” has no save to hook into, which is exactly what a scheduled flow handles.
